title: Kasumi Courier: a cyberpunk delivery game (Out Now on itch)
author: burgric
selftext:
**Kasumi Courier**, a first-person cyberpunk delivery game, is now available to download on itch. You start out on a battered moped, riding through a rain-soaked neon city from 22:00 till dawn, with a satnav, a phone and a CB radio on the dash, delivering parcels against the clock.

**Features:**

* Over 10 hours of story about crime and corruption, with endless nights after it ends (you can end up running the depot)
* Four neon districts to explore
* Five vehicles to unlock
* Two gangs hiding on the radio dial, offering work that pays well and brings trouble
* Weather, police roadblocks, blackouts and gang wars that change your route
* Three radio stations of original music
* Drivers on the CB with their own stories, DJs, news bulletins and song requests
* Bars, a nightclub, flats to rent and own, and a few games on your nights off
* And much more!

**How it was made**

* Development took around 7 weeks. Originally the game began as a browser game, then I decided I wanted it to run as an application.
* The game was originally simple in concept, and then grew exponentially. I began it around mid-late September, created a design doc with Claude and set out what would become the main features and a story arc that lasts around 10 hours.
* I’m a composer, writer and designer rather than a programmer. I directed and designed around 70% of the game, and Claude Pro (Opus 5.5 on Medium) created/designed the rest and wrote the code: about 24,000 lines of JavaScript using three.js, packaged as a Windows app with Electron.
* No AI image generation. Every building, car, character and texture is pixel art drawn in code, so the whole city is built from boxes and tiny canvas textures.
* All the music is synthesised in code with the Web Audio API: three radio stations of original tracks (one is my own composition), plus music for the bars and back rooms. I described each track (style, instruments, mood, structure), listened to renders, and gave notes until I was satisfied.
* The workflow was a loop of describing a feature, testing it, sending screenshots of anything wrong and repeating. A lot of the work was refining visual glitches (typically clipping) in the environment. Most weeks I reached my weekly Claude usage limit by Saturday (refreshing on Sunday).
* The music, screenshots and video files (a handful generated for the trailer) took the longest for Claude to generate. Claude composed and provided some shots as seen in the trailer, while I directed others.
* I curated all of the game's dialogue and writing. Most of what Claude came up with I liked, but some didn't make sense/contradicted what actually happened in the game. So I had to revise a fair amount of the writing.
* The late game content required the most attention, due to choices the player can make and branching consequences.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow, the music, or what worked and what didn’t. Thanks for checking it out!

**Free demo** (the whole first week of the game) is available on the itch page, and the full game is **$2.99 for launch** (40% off) until 19-11-26.
